data.description: Decision (Forrest, 2026-08-30, recorded in CLAUDE.md Operating Modes): sending a message in the chat app should trigger one /advance tick when no agent loop is already running. Goal: the chat app becomes Forrest's primary interface with the company; Claude Code chat recedes to governance/meta. Design constraints discovered so far: (1) The chat app runs only via docker compose (AS-4); a container cannot spawn a claude session on the host, so the trigger needs a HOST-SIDE watcher (launchd agent or supervised script) — keep it tiny. (2) Signal channel: compose bind-mounts ./data, so the server/store can touch a sentinel file (e.g. data/last-human-message) on insert of a message authored by human:* — the host watcher (fswatch or cheap polling) reacts to that; do NOT trigger on agent-authored messages. (3) Single-flight lock shared with the loop: if a /loop or a tick is already active, the watcher no-ops — the running tick's inbox pull delivers the message (suggested: a lockfile the watcher, /advance, and /loop-mode ticks all respect; document it in advance.md). (4) Debounce bursts (10-30s) so a rapid multi-message send fires one tick, not N. (5) Fire via headless invocation: claude -p '/advance' from the repo root; investigate permission-mode requirements for unattended runs and document what the host must have configured. Acceptance: with nothing running, a DM sent from the browser UI produces exactly one tick that reads the inbox and acts; with a loop running, no extra tick fires; agent-authored messages never trigger; watcher survives reboot (launchd) or documents how to start it.

data.body: Sequencing note (board directive, DM msg 50, 2026-08-30): 'lets ship these internal improvements first so we can streamline work later' — the chat-app improvements he named ship ahead of this. Queue as set by the CTO: AS-5 (planned, in flight — finish first), AS-6 (#board hidden channel + typeahead, decision now recorded), AS-8 (employee roster + work status in DM sidebar), then AS-7, then AS-3. Priority stays high — this is still the door to the target operating model; it just isn't next. Also renamed: 'investor' -> 'board member' per current company language.

Planning done (CTO). Design: (1) sentinel apps/chat/data/last-human-message.json written atomically (tmp+rename) from store.postMessage on human:* authors only — covers HTTP+CLI+thread replies, non-fatal on write failure; (2) host watcher apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs, zero-dep node, 5s polling (FSEvents unreliable across bind mounts), 15s trailing debounce, highwater file so messages sent while the watcher was down still fire once; (3) single-flight lock apps/chat/data/advance.lock (pid+startedAt+source; stale = dead pid or >45min), held by the watcher for its ticks, by the tick itself for loop/manual runs (advance.md step-0 wording in plan §10); (4) tick = claude -p '/advance' --permission-mode acceptEdits, 30min hard timeout, logs to apps/chat/data/logs/, highwater advances at fire time so a failed tick never refire-storms — next human message retries; (5) launchd plist template + ops README in repo; actual launchctl install + first live fire are board-assisted acceptance steps (host permission context). Lock is etiquette, not correctness — Lattice claims + SQLite serialize the real state. Ready for implementation.

Implementation done (developer-marcus), 4 commits on feat/AS-7-message-trigger. Built: (1) store.js sentinel — human:*-only, atomic tmp+rename, non-fatal, :memory:-skipped; (2) watch/advance-watcher.mjs — pure decide()/isLockStale() + thin shell: 5s poll, 15s non-extending debounce, highwater-at-fire-time, wx lock w/ staleness (dead pid OR >45min) + one steal retry, 30min TERM->15s->KILL, 14d tick-log pruning, pid single-instance guard; (3) launchd plist template + ops README w/ first-fire checklist; (4) advance.md step-0/step-5 lock wording verbatim from plan §10. Tested: container suite 63 -> 76, all green (4 sentinel tests incl. EISDIR injection; 9 pure watcher tests). Hand-walked safely: sentinel on a COPY of chat.db (agent post no-op, human post exact JSON), and a fully sandboxed watcher run (fake repo root, stub claude) — recovery fire, correct argv, lock released, second instance refused, clean SIGTERM. Deviation (boring choice): Dockerfile now COPYs watch/ so the mountless test service can import decide(); watch/ never executes in-container. decide() carries a debounceUntil field beyond the plan's loose signature — needed for pure non-extending-window tests. QA should attack: debounce edge timing in decide(), lock steal race in acquireLock(), tick-log stream lifecycle (spawn-error path), README install steps vs plist placeholders. Residual board-assisted acceptance: plan §11 crit. 7-10 (launchd install/reboot, first live fire + permission-denial watch, loop-lock no-op, killed-tick recovery) — checklist is in apps/chat/watch/README.md. NOT done here by design: no watcher run against the live system, no real claude invocation, no plist installed.

REVIEW (qa-priya, cold): PASS — no rework needed, no inline fixes needed. Inputs: plan file, git diff master...feat/AS-7-message-trigger read cold, container suite run myself, sandboxed attack harness (scratchpad fake repo + stub claude; live system and real claude never touched, per plan §12).

SUITE: docker compose run --rm --build test -> 76 pass / 0 fail, matching the implementer's claim (63 -> 76 = 4 sentinel + 9 watcher tests).

NODE-TESTABLE CRITERIA (plan §11):
1. PASS — human post writes exact {messageId, authorId, conversationId, createdAt}; second post overwrites; tmp renamed away (store.test.js deepEqual, witnessed green in-container).
2. PASS — agent/system/ingestEvent never touch the sentinel; source confirms ingestEvent inserts directly as system identity, and registerIdentity regex (^(human|agent|system):[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$) + kind-prefix check make the author.startsWith('human:') gate authoritative.
3. PASS — human thread reply updates sentinel (test witnessed).
4. PASS — :memory: never writes; injected EISDIR write failure does not fail the post (equivalent failure injection for the generic catch — accepted). tx() rethrows on ROLLBACK and the sentinel write sits after tx return, so a rolled-back post can never write a sentinel (source-verified).
5. PASS — all six named decide() cases covered in watcher.test.js; plus 18 additional QA edge probes all pass: sentinel == highwater -> noop; fire at exactly debounceUntil (strict <); future-dated lock treated fresh (clock-skew-safe, never stale-by-age); corrupt highwater ({}, NaN, string) degrades to at most one refire, never a wedge or throw; Infinity/garbage messageId -> no-sentinel noop; unparsable-lock -> stolen with 'unparsable' reason; staleness boundary strict-> at exactly 45min still fresh; clock stepped backward mid-window -> waits, no throw.
6. PASS — full suite green in-container; watcher tests import pure logic only (mountless invariant held; Dockerfile COPY watch/ is test-import-only, commented, no CMD change — deviation accepted).

ATTACK RESULTS (sandboxed shell, all pass): spawn failure (bad claude bin) -> ERROR logged, spawn-error line in tick log, lock RELEASED, highwater advanced (no refire storm); malformed lock JSON -> STEAL logged with reason, fire proceeds, lock released on exit; fresh foreign lock (live pid) -> SKIP lock-fresh-loop, zero fires while held, immediate fire after release with NO second debounce wait; second watcher instance -> FATAL + exit 1; pid file removed on SIGTERM (an apparent failure here was my harness racing the signal handler — retested clean); argv audit: child argv is exactly [-p /advance --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format text], no user-controlled string reaches it (message bodies never read; authorId charset-locked by identity regex, only ever logged); child env is exactly {PATH, HOME} — injected parent secret did NOT leak; stdout/stderr streamed to tick log. Concurrent sentinel writers (2 processes x 200 posts, shared dir): valid JSON sentinel, zero tmp orphans, no crash.

advance.md WORDING: step-0, step-5 append, and Running-continuously bullet verified verbatim against plan §10 by normalized string compare; sole delta is bold-marker placement adapting the blockquote to a numbered list item ('0. **Take...**' vs '**0. Take...**') — word-for-word identical otherwise. Verbatim claim upheld.

DEVIATIONS ACCEPTED: Dockerfile COPY watch/ (above); decide() debounceUntil in/out field beyond plan signature (required for pure non-extending-window tests, documented).

NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -> filed as backlog task AS-13 (none violates a stated criterion): stale-lock double-steal race (plan §5 sanctions: lock is etiquette, not correctness), fixed sentinel tmp name across processes, SIGKILL grace timer vs mutable child var (reachable only with ADVANCE_DEBOUNCE_S set below the 15s kill grace), SKIP-line log chatter during long foreign ticks, pid-guard TOCTOU.

BOARD-ASSISTED RESIDUAL (explicitly deferred, does NOT block done per plan §11/§12): criteria 7-10 — launchd install + reboot survival (7), first live fire exactly-one-tick + permission-denial watch (8), loop-lock no-extra-tick (9), killed-tick recovery (10). Runbook coverage verified: apps/chat/watch/README.md First-fire checklist items 1-4 map one-to-one to criteria 7-10 with plan references; install/uninstall, permission-mode reality (denied-not-waited), troubleshooting, Linux ownership caveat, node>=20 check, and all three plist placeholders (__REPO_ROOT__, __NODE_BIN__, __PATH__) rendered by the documented sed. Board records results as a lattice comment on AS-7 when performed.

RECOMMENDATION: meets all node-testable acceptance criteria; orchestrator may move AS-7 to done. PHILOSOPHY check: zero external calls (local spawn only), no spend beyond tick tokens, at-most-once-per-message firing prevents unbounded burn.

First-fire results (post-done ops verification, board-installed per runbook, 2026-08-30): [1] Install: PASS — launchd job loaded, state=running, START logged with expected config line. [2] First trigger: watcher logic PASS, tick FAIL — human message (messageId 120) produced exactly one DEBOUNCE->FIRE->EXIT cycle, lock taken and released, highwater advanced to 120; but the spawned tick died in ~2s with 'Not logged in - Please run /login'. Diagnosis (orchestrator-verified with env -i tests): claude auth is macOS-Keychain-based and requires USER in the child environment; our fire() spawns with env exactly {PATH, HOME} per the plan's minimal-env rule — one variable too strict. 'env -i HOME=... USER=... PATH=... claude -p' works; dropping USER reproduces the failure. [3] Loop-suppression check: PENDING. [4] Reboot-survival check: PENDING. Fix filed as a separate bug task (child env must add USER; see new task). Note the at-most-once design behaved as intended: highwater advanced at FIRE, so the failed tick did not refire in a loop — the next human message will retry naturally once the env fix lands.

First-fire shakeout, checklist item 2 update (cto-owen): the AS-14 re-fire authenticated successfully — and then exposed bug #2, a lock-protocol deadlock. The watcher takes advance.lock (source:"watcher", its own pid 17730) BEFORE spawning claude -p '/advance'; the spawned tick's step-0 etiquette sees a fresh foreign-looking lock and self-cancels. Evidence: apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T18-08-30.241Z.log — tick exited 0 with 'Tick ended as a no-op — lock is held', lock holder pid == live watcher pid. Root cause: advance.md step 0 says watcher-fired ticks skip the lock check, but the spawned tick has no way to KNOW it is watcher-fired ('claude -p /advance' is byte-identical to a manual invocation), so the exemption is undetectable and every watcher-fired tick self-cancels. Item 2 status: fired + authenticated + self-cancelled on lock etiquette. Fix task filed separately (bug, high).

First-fire shakeout, item 2, third attempt (tick-2026-08-30T18-20-03.664Z.log): AUTHENTICATED (AS-14 fix confirmed working) but self-cancelled — the headless permission layer declined the env read, so the tick could not see ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT and correctly treated its parent watcher lock as foreign per the AS-15 step-0 rule. Transport fix filed as AS-20 (prompt-argument marker: claude -p '/advance watcher:<pid>'; env var stays as belt). Also for the record: that tick log's 'watcher re-fired message 120 three times / highwater bug' analysis is a misdiagnosis from missing context — the repeats were deliberate board-side highwater resets during debugging; no highwater task is warranted.
